daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The KPK issued six SP3 terminations for corruption cases, including one involving the DPR Secretary General. The move marks a significant development in the anti-corruption body's case management. This comes alongside other investigative actions as the KPK continues to examine various corruption cases across the country.

  • The KPK examined an active police officer to investigate extortion practices allegedly committed against the Pemalang regent.
  • Golkar Secretary General stated parties must conduct early training following corruption cases involving regional heads.
  • Golkar Chairman Bahlil said Golkar's political work will begin next year.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs unveiled a new method to ensure social assistance recipients are accurately targeted.
  • Commission IX of the DPR targets completion of the initial draft of the Employment Bill this week.
  • The Attorney General's Office examined four witnesses and searched locations related to the money laundering case of Febrie Adriansyah.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo hosted Thai Prime Minister Anutin in the first official visit by a Thai PM to Indonesia in 15 years. The leaders set a target of US$20 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 and adopted a strategic partnership roadmap to 2030. Both countries also launched new flight routes to boost tourism.

  • The Royal Thai Armed Forces awarded an honorary military decoration to President Prabowo, whom Thai military officials described as a "military icon".
  • Thailand committed to supply 36 amphibious armored vehicles for Indonesia's Marine Corps.
  • Indonesia and Thailand agreed to strengthen cooperation against transnational crime, with PM Anutin telling Prabowo that Thailand had rescued 1,000 Indonesian scam victims.
  • President Prabowo offered condolences on the passing of Thai Princess Bajrakitiyabha.
  • The Foreign Ministry confirmed no Indonesians were affected by a 5.6 magnitude earthquake in Egypt.

Other

The head of BGN (the new school meal authority) said mass food poisoning in Semarang occurred because the supplier did not follow standard operating procedures, after 707 people were poisoned. BGN subsequently suspended the supplier in Semarang. The Constitutional Court separately ruled that the MBG program must be supported by adequate and dedicated budget.

  • The government is preparing a funding scheme for the mandatory E10 bioethanol-blended gasoline program, while Energy Minister Bahlil said NMC battery incentives are a key strategy to boost the nickel-based electric vehicle market.
  • The Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK) projected Indonesia's economy to grow up to 6 percent, describing the economy as resilient.
  • Indonesia and Thailand agreed to strengthen food security cooperation, with PM Anutin asking Prabowo to import rice, meat, and milk from Thailand in exchange for buying Indonesian fertilizer.
  • OJK assured over 100 global investors of capital market reforms.
  • BP BUMN and Danantara are drafting a five-year strategic roadmap for state-owned enterprise transformation.
